transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-23 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rivera (Redwood SE), Samira Patel (Quantum Head of Search), Tom Nguyen (ML Eng), Olivia Brooks (CTO)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough for embeddings + reranking. Focus on relevance pipeline, cost/latency tradeoffs, and security questions (SSO/SAML, data retention). Agreed to pilot and benchmarking next week.

Topics: hosted embeddings, embeddings dimensionality, vector store compatibility, reranker endpoint, Redwood Console metrics, Optimize suggestions (batching/quant), security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), pilot plan and success metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, i see samira and team, welcome.
[00:16] Samira: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we run search for 800 stores and want faster relevant product results, latency matters but so does cost.
[00:30] Diego: quick agenda, we'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint, how to do nearest neighbor, then the rerank endpoint and tie it into the console for monitoring and Optimize suggestions.
[00:45] Tom: couple of constraints — we use an internal vector store but can try pinecone, also need SSO and audit logs, olivia has compliance questions.
[00:58] Olivia: yes, SOC two and SAML is must, also data residency in eu for some skus.
[01:12] Maya: totally, we have SOC2 report and SAML SSO, we'll share the security whitepaper and a link to the private deployment options, but for this pilot hosted should work with egress and region controls. (note: link in chat: /security/whitepaper.pdf)
[01:35] Samira: can you show the reranker flow? we currently do 2-stage: dense recall from faiss then lexical rerank and it's a mess.
[01:50] Diego: yep — so first we call embeddings endpoint, we support 1536 and 1024 dims depending on model, then you do ANN — we show results, then call reranker with context + candidate list, it returns scored list. i'll demo with sample product Q&A.
[02:12] [screen share starts] Diego: here in the console, API explorer, call generate embeddings curl example — you can see token counts and cost estimate inline.
[02:30] Tom: quick question, what's the latencies for 1k dims on hosted?
[02:40] Diego: median 45-120ms per embedding depending on model and batch size for small batches, for our gpt-type reranker it's about 120-300ms per call but we do continuous batching and can get to 80ms p50 with optimal batching. sometimes the transcript shows KV cash instead of cache but we handle kv cache in runtime.
[03:05] Samira: ok that's promising. cost wise?
[03:10] Maya: i'll send pricing tiers, high level: embeddings priced per 1k vectors, rerank per call plus token usage. Optimize will make batching recs to reduce per-token cost.
[03:30] Tom: do you support custom scoring or only pairwise rerank?
[03:36] Diego: currently our reranker supports listwise and pairwise scoring — you can pass features and metadata; there's an examples folder in the repo. for complex pipelines we recommend reranker as second stage after ANN.
[03:58] Samira: what about vector store compatibility? we use an in-house system.
[04:05] Diego: we export embeddings as floats, you can choose 32/16 bit and quantized formats for smaller footprint. works with faiss, milvus, pinecone, qdrant, or you can host in your own index and call our rerank API with candidate ids.
[04:28] Olivia: security — where do tokens live? KMS?
[04:33] Maya: we encrypt customer data at rest, integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, and hosted uses our KMS with customer tenant separation. will share SOC2 and SOC2 type II snapshot and KMS integration doc.
[04:52] Samira: any regulator issues for eu?
[04:56] Maya: we have eu regions and options to keep logs in region; for strict data residency we also have private deployment.
[05:10] Tom: can we run a quick sample? i uploaded a small corpus in the worksheet beforehand?
[05:17] Diego: yes i'll run the demo using the sample 200 product Q&A you sent — show embeddings similarity then reranker boosting.
[05:30] [demo run, audio shows some typing]
[06:02] Diego: initial recall results, you can see baseline before rerank, we then call rerank endpoint with candidates payload — note the payload limit and token math, it's in the API docs.
[06:27] Samira: hmm i see the top result moved, that was unexpected but better. latency spikes a bit — what's the batching window?
[06:40] Diego: default batching is adaptive; Optimize suggests a small batch of 8 for yours given qps. we can tune target SLOs per route.
[06:55] Tom: logs — can i get per-route token breakdown?
[07:00] Maya: yes console shows token-level cost and per-route latency. we'll give you a demo account so you can poke around.
[07:20] Olivia: auditors will want audit trail — is there immutable logs?
[07:26] Maya: we capture request traces and exportable audit logs, retention configurable with enterprise plan.
[07:44] Samira: what's the rollback story if a model degrades?
[07:49] Diego: console has rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper or more stable model variant. you can tag a stable candidate and enable canary.
[08:03] Tom: curious about quantization — does it affect ranking quality?
[08:10] Diego: yes slightly, Optimize will suggest quant profiles: q4_0 for 8-bit-ish or q8 for more aggressive. we can run A/B to measure mmr or nDCG change.
[08:30] [slight crosstalk] Samira: okay so pilot plan: we want 10k queries/day, measure p@10 and latency 95th under 400ms.
[08:43] Maya: sounds good, we'll draft success metrics in the pilot SOW.
[09:00] Diego: i'll prepare the benchmark harness — quick note, sometimes transcribers show Redwood dedicate instead of Dedicated, just ignore the little typos.
[09:18] Samira: any blockers for us to start next week?
[09:23] Maya: just SSO info and sample corpus. olivia — anything from compliance?
[09:29] Olivia: once i see the SOC2 and retention options i'm ok to proceed. also want agreement on data deletion post-pilot.
[09:40] Maya: we can include a retention clause.
[09:45] Tom: about the reranker input, can we add click-features?
[09:50] Diego: yes you can pass numerical features as part of the candidate payload, we normalize on server side.
[10:05] [demo wrap-up] Maya: recap — we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark harness, and set up a pilot. diego will run a focused rerank benchmark on your sample.
[10:20] Samira: great, thanks. one more request: can you show logging for an example rerank call in the console?
[10:27] Diego: sure, switching to logs, here you can filter by model, route, and see token-level breakdown per request.
[10:45] Olivia: ok that helps.
[11:00] Maya: any final Qs?
[11:05] Samira: no, we're good. excited to try the pilot.
[11:12] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invite for kickoff and an email with links. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
